title: Nova Systems v. Solis Logistics

parties.name: Nova Systems Ltd
parties.description: Commercial electronics manufacturer seeking damages for defective components and delayed delivery.

parties.name: Solis Logistics Corp
parties.description: Logistics and freight distribution carrier contesting liability based on force majeure and lack of timely notice.

agreed_facts: On March 1, 2025, Nova Systems and Solis Logistics executed a Master Freight Agreement for commercial component deliveries.
The contract required Solis Logistics to deliver 5,000 optical sensors to Nova Systems' assembly facility in humidity-sealed containers by May 15, 2025.
Solis Logistics experienced logistical delays and delivered the consignment on June 2, 2025, eighteen days past the agreed deadline.
Upon arrival, 1,200 optical sensors were found to have suffered moisture ingress and failed quality assurance testing.
Nova Systems notified Solis Logistics of the damaged goods within forty-eight hours of delivery.

documents.title: Master Freight Agreement
documents.description: Commercial agreement establishing delivery timelines, temperature monitoring specifications, and claim notice procedures.

documents.title: Bill of Lading and Delivery Confirmation
documents.description: Receiving report documenting moisture damage to outer cartons and serial numbers of affected sensor units.

documents.title: Notice of Formal Claim
documents.description: Written notice issued by Nova Systems demanding replacement value and consequential business disruption costs.

witnesses.name: Elena Rostova
witnesses.role: Director of Procurement, Nova Systems Ltd
witnesses.background: Supervised component intake and conducted the post-delivery damage assessment.
witnesses.statement_summary: Testifies that prompt arrival of intact optical sensors was vital to production, and that container seals showed visible moisture upon opening.

witnesses.name: Marcus Vance
witnesses.role: Head of Fleet Operations, Solis Logistics Corp
witnesses.background: Managed the transit schedule and carrier dispatch for shipment #SL-884.
witnesses.statement_summary: Testifies that transit delays were caused by severe regional weather conditions beyond reasonable control, and asserts cargo was handed over to warehouse staff without immediate objection.

legal_issues: Whether the eighteen-day delivery delay constituted a material breach under the terms of the Master Freight Agreement.
Whether the carrier failed to maintain agreed environmental protections during transit resulting in cargo damage.
Whether the Claimant fulfilled its commercial duty to inspect and mitigate upon receipt of non-conforming goods.
